00253.purpose: After early breast cancer treatment, endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence. In advanced disease, the aim is to control cancer and symptoms. Your setting determines the duration and follow-up.
00253.indication_text: Adjuvant or advanced oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer in pre- or postmenopausal women, within the exact NCCP eligibility criteria.
00253.administration_text: Swallow the tablet whole, with or without food. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not replace it; take the next scheduled daily dose.
00253.monitoring_summary: Before treatment, check blood count, kidney and liver function, clot history, medicines and pregnancy possibility. The current Irish Tamox product information also recommends an eye examination before treatment and regular blood-count, liver and calcium checks; the team agrees their timing for your product. ECG and electrolyte checks depend on heart-rhythm risks or symptoms. NCCP recommends an annual gynaecological examination. Report unusual vaginal bleeding or visual changes promptly.
00253.urgent_extra: Get urgent help for a swollen painful leg, chest pain, new breathlessness, stroke symptoms, fainting with palpitations, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe blistering rash. Tell the team promptly about unusual vaginal bleeding, visual changes, jaundice, unusual bruising or symptoms that make treatment difficult.
00253.consent_support: Discuss the expected benefit in your treatment setting alongside clot, womb, eye and liver risks and effects on daily life. Tell the team about previous clots, severe liver disease and all other medicines. Tamoxifen is not contraception: discuss an effective non-hormonal method during treatment and for nine months after stopping, where relevant. Absent periods do not prove infertility. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are excluded from this NCCP pathway. Do not change antidepressants, blood thinners or other regular medicines yourself.

support.title: Help with daily treatment
support.text: Ask early for help with flushes, sweats, sleep, mood, vaginal or sexual symptoms, nausea or fatigue. A difficult side effect matters even if it is not medically severe. The team can discuss symptom treatment and the endocrine plan.

support.title: Support medicines
support.text: This oral hormone treatment does not require routine steroid premedication, injections to raise white cells or a standard anti-sickness course. Symptom medicines are chosen individually and checked for interactions.

support.title: Bloods, eyes and reviews
support.text: Agree who arranges the recommended eye and blood checks, their due windows and who reviews the results. Report bleeding or visual changes between appointments.

support.title: Bone and activity
support.text: The effect on bone differs before and after menopause. Discuss your own fracture risks and whether a bone-density test is appropriate; activity and bone care should suit your circumstances.

sections.title: Make one daily dose easier
sections.text: Link the tablet to a regular daily routine. Ask the pharmacy for help with supply or swallowing difficulties. Do not double a dose to catch up.

sections.title: Surgery, immobility and clot risk
sections.text: Tell the surgical and oncology teams that you take tamoxifen. They decide whether any temporary interruption is needed; there is no automatic fixed interruption for everyone.

sections.title: Bleeding and eye symptoms
sections.text: Do not wait for an annual review to report unusual vaginal bleeding or visual disturbance. An annual gynaecological examination does not mean routine ultrasound or biopsy for an asymptomatic person.

sections.title: Review all medicines
sections.text: Review prescriptions, supplements and over-the-counter products, including antidepressants, blood thinners and hormone preparations. Some reduce formation of active endoxifen or add bleeding or heart-rhythm risks. Do not stop an essential medicine yourself; ask oncology pharmacy to reconcile the complete list.

sections.title: Match the checks to your product
sections.text: Ask which tamoxifen product you receive and agree its blood and eye monitoring plan. ECG timing follows your risks, symptoms and the relevant product information.

questions.q: Do I have a treatment-free week?
questions.a: Take tamoxifen once daily continuously. There is no planned week off. The prescriber confirms the duration for the treatment setting.

questions.q: When are bloods, ECGs or echoes needed?
questions.a: Before treatment, check blood count, kidney and liver function, clot history, medicines and pregnancy possibility. The current Irish Tamox product information also recommends an eye examination before treatment and regular blood-count, liver and calcium checks; the team agrees their timing for your product. ECG and electrolyte checks depend on heart-rhythm risks or symptoms. NCCP recommends an annual gynaecological examination. Report unusual vaginal bleeding or visual changes promptly. There is no routine echo schedule for tamoxifen alone.

After curative treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. The mastectomy side is not routinely mammographed. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended for asymptomatic early-breast surveillance. New symptoms need assessment between appointments. For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Indolent disease may be reviewed less often; new symptoms can prompt earlier scans. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not a universal three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.
Discuss your menopausal state and personal fracture risks. Tamoxifen can affect bone differently before and after menopause. Your team will advise whether a bone-density test is needed.

For early breast cancer, discuss the initial endocrine course and a later decision about extending or changing treatment; some patients continue endocrine therapy to 10 years. Advanced treatment continues according to benefit and tolerance. A five-year review is not an automatic instruction to stop.

questions.q: Do I need a port or home pump?
questions.a: No port or home infusion pump is needed for this medicine itself. Any separately prescribed medicine has its own access requirements.

questions.q: Can I keep taking my other medicines?
questions.a: Give the team a complete list, including antidepressants, blood thinners, hormone preparations and supplements. A pharmacist will check whether changes are needed. Do not stop a regular medicine yourself.

questions.q: What if side effects make me want to stop?
questions.a: Contact the team early. Help with symptoms or a review of the endocrine plan may make treatment easier. Do not wait until you miss several doses to ask for support.

evidence.title: Why tamoxifen is offered
evidence.population: People with oestrogen-receptor-positive early breast cancer in randomized studies.
evidence.interpretation: Taking the planned course after early breast cancer reduces the chance of the cancer returning and lowers the risk of dying from breast cancer. A longer course may bring further benefit for some people.
evidence.limitations: The size of the benefit depends on your cancer, previous treatment and remaining risk. Early-breast study results do not predict how an individual with advanced breast cancer will respond. Longer treatment also carries risks and should be reviewed with the team.

chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: After early breast cancer treatment, endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence. In advanced disease, the aim is to control cancer and symptoms. Your setting determines the duration and follow-up.

items.title: Who this card covers
items.text: Adjuvant or advanced oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer in pre- or postmenopausal women, within the exact NCCP eligibility criteria.

items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: 20 mg orally once daily. Swallow the tablet whole, with or without food. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not replace it; take the next scheduled daily dose.

items.title: Duration and decision points
items.text: For early breast cancer, discuss the initial endocrine course and a later decision about extending or changing treatment; some patients continue endocrine therapy to 10 years. Advanced treatment continues according to benefit and tolerance. A five-year review is not an automatic instruction to stop.

items.title: Individual safety
items.text: History of significant thromboembolic disease is an NCCP exclusion. Severe hepatic impairment is not recommended. Interactions, including potent CYP2D6 inhibitors, need medication review.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Baseline, ongoing safety checks and cancer scans have different purposes.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: Check blood count, kidney and liver function, medicines, clot history and pregnancy possibility. The current Irish Tamox information also recommends an eye examination before treatment.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: NCCP uses clinically indicated liver, clotting, eye and ECG tests and an annual gynaecological examination. Current Irish Tamox information additionally calls for regular blood counts, liver and calcium checks. Agree their timing with your team.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: ECG and electrolyte checks depend on rhythm risks, other medicines and symptoms. Your prescribed product and clinical team determine repeat timing; there is no routine echo schedule for tamoxifen alone.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Tamoxifen may lower bone density before menopause and can help maintain it after menopause. Your own fracture risks and menopausal state guide whether a bone-density scan is needed.

chapters.title: Your setting changes the pathway
chapters.intro: Choose the pathway that your team has confirmed; these are not all extra treatments you must have.

items.title: Early-breast follow-up
items.text: After curative treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. The mastectomy side is not routinely mammographed. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended for asymptomatic early-breast surveillance. New symptoms need assessment between appointments.

items.title: Surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy
items.text: In an early-breast pathway, chemotherapy, if indicated, precedes endocrine treatment. Surgery and its pathology guide adjuvant choices. Postoperative radiotherapy is usually delivered after recovery and any adjuvant chemotherapy; aromatase inhibitors may overlap radiotherapy under the agreed plan. Tamoxifen timing around radiotherapy is agreed by the treating teams. None of these additional treatments is automatically required by an endocrine prescription.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Indolent disease may be reviewed less often; new symptoms can prompt earlier scans. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not a universal three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: Tumour markers may supplement imaging and clinical assessment in advanced disease if they are informative, especially if elevated at baseline. They do not replace scans, and a marker change alone should not determine treatment failure. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: Menopause, pregnancy and contraception
items.text: Tamoxifen is not contraception. Discuss an effective non-hormonal method during treatment and for nine months after stopping, where relevant. Absent periods do not prove infertility. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are excluded from this NCCP pathway.

chapters.title: Reviewing the duration of treatment
chapters.intro: The findings guide a discussion with your team; they do not predict one person’s outcome.

items.title: A planned discussion about continuing
items.text: Some people benefit from taking tamoxifen for longer after early breast cancer. The decision weighs the remaining risk of recurrence against side effects, clot and womb risks, other conditions and your preferences. Do not stop at a review milestone without discussing the plan.

00361.purpose: The aim is to control advanced hormone-sensitive breast cancer and its symptoms, with response and tolerability reviewed before continuing.
00361.indication_text: This NCCP monotherapy pathway covers postmenopausal women with ER-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has relapsed or progressed on or after adjuvant anti-oestrogen treatment. Fulvestrant prescribed with capivasertib or a CDK4/6 medicine follows a separate combination regimen.
00361.administration_text: Each usual 500 mg dose is given as two 5 mL injections, one in each buttock, slowly over one to two minutes per injection. This is not an intravenous infusion; no port or pump is needed for fulvestrant itself.
00361.monitoring_summary: Before treatment, check blood count, kidney and liver function, the menopausal and treatment history, pregnancy exclusion and bleeding risk. Before injections, tell staff about anticoagulants, bruising, bleeding or previous nerve symptoms. Repeat liver tests when indicated; scans follow the agreed cancer-control plan. Tell anyone ordering an oestrogen blood test that you receive fulvestrant because some tests can give a misleadingly high result.
00361.urgent_extra: Tell the team about unusual bleeding or extensive bruising, injection-site pain with numbness or pain down the leg, jaundice or worsening symptoms. Severe chest pain, breathlessness or stroke symptoms require emergency help.
00361.consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, injection discomfort and possible nerve injury, bleeding or bruising, liver effects, flushes, joint symptoms and fatigue. Liver impairment or an existing modified dose requires an agreed prescriber and pharmacy plan. Where relevant, use effective contraception during treatment and for two years after the final dose under the EMA product information. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are excluded. Tell staff about blood thinners; do not stop them yourself.

support.title: Make injection visits manageable
support.text: Discuss injection discomfort, flushes, joint or muscle symptoms, fatigue and nausea. Ask early for symptom help or practical support attending appointments.

support.title: Support medicines
support.text: Fulvestrant alone does not require routine steroid premedication, injections to raise white cells or a standard anti-sickness course. A combination medicine can add its own supportive-care needs.

support.title: Bleeding and nerve symptoms
support.text: Tell staff about blood thinners, unusual bruising or bleeding before an injection. Severe buttock pain, new numbness, weakness or pain down the leg needs prompt assessment.

support.title: Tests and appointments
support.text: Confirm the extra loading visit and later appointments, who books required blood tests and scans, and who reviews the results. Tell the laboratory team about fulvestrant if an oestrogen blood test is ordered.

sections.title: The first month is different
sections.text: There is an extra injection visit two weeks after the first dose. After the Day 29 dose, visits continue every 28 days. Ask the team to confirm each appointment.

sections.title: Before an injection
sections.text: Tell staff about anticoagulants, unusual bleeding or bruising. Do not stop an anticoagulant yourself. The team reviews injection safety and any dose modification.

sections.title: Injection technique and aftercare
sections.text: Staff give deep intramuscular gluteal injections slowly. Report severe pain, numbness or pain radiating down the leg promptly.

sections.title: If a visit is delayed
sections.text: Contact the clinic to agree the next date. Do not calculate a catch-up or extra dose from this reference graphic; dose scheduling remains the clinical team’s responsibility.

sections.title: Other cancer medicines
sections.text: If you also receive capivasertib or a CDK4/6 medicine, use the full combination plan for tablets, safety checks and side-effect advice. Fulvestrant-alone information cannot replace it.

sections.title: Oestrogen blood tests
sections.text: Tell the clinician and laboratory that you receive fulvestrant. Some antibody-based tests can read falsely high; the team should confirm how a result was measured before changing treatment.

questions.a: The usual schedule is Day 1, Day 15 and Day 29, then every 28 days. The first month includes an extra loading visit. Follow your clinic appointments; contact the team if a visit is missed.

questions.q: When are bloods, ECGs or echoes needed?
questions.a: Before treatment, check blood count, kidney and liver function, the menopausal and treatment history, pregnancy exclusion and bleeding risk. Before injections, tell staff about anticoagulants, bruising, bleeding or previous nerve symptoms. Repeat liver tests when indicated; scans follow the agreed cancer-control plan. Tell anyone ordering an oestrogen blood test that you receive fulvestrant because some tests can give a misleadingly high result. There is no routine ECG or echo schedule for fulvestrant alone; a companion medicine may need additional checks.

For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Indolent disease may be reviewed less often; new symptoms can prompt earlier scans. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not a universal three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.
Assess personal fracture and osteoporosis risk. Fulvestrant does not carry an automatic AI DXA timetable; agree testing and repeat intervals when indicated.
Continue while the treatment is beneficial and tolerated, with planned response reviews. There is no fixed adjuvant five-year course on this card.

questions.q: Do I need a port or home pump?
questions.a: No port or home infusion pump is needed for this medicine itself. Any separately prescribed medicine has its own access requirements.

questions.q: Is this the same plan as capivasertib with fulvestrant?
questions.a: No. The injections are part of both plans, but capivasertib adds its own tablet schedule, selection requirements, blood-sugar checks and side-effect care. Use the full combination plan if both are prescribed.

questions.q: Why might an oestrogen test need checking?
questions.a: Fulvestrant can interfere with some laboratory tests and make the result look higher than it is. Tell the team about treatment so they can check the test method before making a treatment decision.

evidence.title: Why fulvestrant is offered
evidence.population: Postmenopausal people with hormone-sensitive advanced breast cancer studied in endocrine-treatment trials.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Control of cancer progression and survival, evaluated separately.
evidence.interpretation: Fulvestrant can help control advanced hormone-sensitive breast cancer. Studies support the usual treatment schedule, while the choice of treatment depends on previous endocrine therapy and the individual cancer.
evidence.limitations: A study comparing fulvestrant doses does not show that monotherapy is better than modern combination treatment. A separate study in people who had not received endocrine therapy found longer control of progression but no proven overall-survival advantage over anastrozole. These findings do not predict an individual outcome.

items.title: Previous endocrine treatment matters
items.text: The team weighs previous treatment, hormone sensitivity, disease extent, other conditions and your priorities when selecting fulvestrant alone or as part of a combination. Studies in people starting their first endocrine treatment do not automatically apply after earlier endocrine therapy.

00253.mechanism: Selective oestrogen-receptor modulator with antagonist activity in breast tissue and tissue-dependent partial agonism elsewhere. Tamoxifen and active metabolites compete at ER. CYP3A4 mainly forms N-desmethyltamoxifen, which CYP2D6 converts to endoxifen; avoid empiric dose escalation for interactions. Tissue-specific action explains uterine stimulation and differing pre/postmenopausal bone effects.
00253.rationale: NCCP includes ER-positive adjuvant and advanced disease before or after menopause. Adjuvant duration is an individualized initial/extended endocrine plan; advanced duration depends on response and tolerability. Do not infer prevention, male breast cancer or a modern combination indication from this NCCP card.

monitoring_source_split.nccp: Baseline FBC, renal and LFT. ECG if clinically indicated. Later ophthalmology, INR, LFT and ECG if indicated. Annual gynaecological examination. No universal repeat FBC, calcium or fixed ECG timing is specified in NCCP.
monitoring_source_split.irish_rowex_2026: Baseline ophthalmology; regular FBC including platelets, LFT and serum calcium, without fixed frequency. ECG/electrolytes guided by QT risk or symptoms.
monitoring_source_split.uk_comparison_only: Some UK product information specifies a repeat QT-risk ECG at steady state after at least four weeks and contraindicates concurrent anastrozole. These must not be silently attributed to current Irish Rowex/NCCP.

00253.organ_function: NCCP: no expected renal/dialysis adjustment; no mild/moderate hepatic adjustment; severe hepatic impairment not recommended. Do not invent creatinine, AST, bilirubin or generic toxicity dose ladders.
00253.medication_safety: Avoid potent CYP2D6 inhibitors where possible; CYP3A4 inducer review, no empirical dose increase. Irish Rowex says oestrogen preparations should not be combined and cautions against platelet-aggregation inhibitors; review essential antiplatelets rather than advising abrupt withdrawal. Coumarin potentiation needs careful monitoring; breast-cancer treatment is not the prevention contraindication. Irish AI combination wording is lack of added benefit; preserve sequential switching.
00253.surgery_vte: NCCP significant prior thromboembolic disease is excluded. Acute/suspected VTE requires urgent management and withholding. Perioperative interruption is individualized to thrombosis risk and cancer-treatment trade-off; no universal stop interval is imposed.
00253.contraception: Current Irish Rowex/Viatris: effective contraception during and for 9 months after treatment in women; product male advice is 6 months but NCCP00253 scope here is women. Non-hormonal method discussion, pregnancy/BF exclusions, amenorrhoea does not establish infertility.

00361.mechanism: Selective ER degrader: competitive ER antagonism with affinity comparable to oestradiol, reduced ER protein and ER-driven transcription, without the partial agonist activity characteristic of tamoxifen. IM depot provides prolonged absorption; the additional Day 15 dose increases exposure during initiation.
00361.rationale: NCCP00361: postmenopausal ER-positive locally advanced/metastatic disease relapsed/progressed on or after adjuvant anti-oestrogen therapy, ECOG0–2. EMA also contains endocrine-naive and combination indications, which do not broaden this exact monotherapy pathway. Critical visceral disease has not been studied in the EMA caution; this is not a contraindication to every visceral metastasis.
00361.schedule: 500 mg IM on Days 1 and 15 of cycle 1, then Day 1 every 28 days: absolute Days 1, 15, 29, 57, 85. Two 5 mL gluteal injections at the usual 500 mg dose, one in each buttock over 1–2 minutes each. Separate injection technique and modified-dose plan from standard schedule.
00361.hepatic_source_conflict: NCCP Table 1: Child-Pugh A no adjustment; B 50% of original dose (250 mg); C not recommended. Current EMA: no adjustment mild/moderate with caution; severe contraindicated. Explicitly block numeric recommendation for B and require consultant/pharmacy reconciliation. Current modified dose must not automatically reset to 500 mg from a renal no-adjustment result.
00361.renal: CrCl ≥30 mL/min no adjustment. <30/dialysis no adjustment expected in NCCP but data limited and caution/review required.
00361.injection: Caution with bleeding diathesis, thrombocytopenia or anticoagulation. No NCCP platelet cutoff or automatic anticoagulant-stop rule. Injection-related neuropathic symptoms require review; use care to avoid sciatic nerve.
00361.monitoring: Baseline FBC/renal/LFT; repeat LFT when clinically indicated; clinical symptom and individualized disease assessment. No invented routine cycle FBC, QT/echo, DPD, G-CSF or steroid premedication requirements for monotherapy.
00361.assay_interference: Structural similarity to oestradiol can cause falsely elevated antibody-based oestradiol immunoassay results. Verify assay suitability with laboratory before inferring ovarian activity or endocrine failure.
00361.interaction_scope: EMA fulvestrant alone needs no adjustment with CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors. This must not clear capivasertib or CDK4/6 companion interactions; full 00947 is a separate pathway.
00361.contraception: EMA: effective contraception during treatment and for 2 years after final dose for women of childbearing potential; pregnancy and breastfeeding contraindicated.

integration_notes: Replace evidence and chapters as entire values so old numerical trial prose is removed. Patient evidence remains qualitative; all numeric trial results belong only in clinician evidence.
Patient updates preserve stable protocol identities, schedule kinds and baseline longitudinal setting-specific follow-up; these are not all new monitoring requirements.
Tamoxifen monitoring distinguishes NCCP from current Irish product supplements; no blanket four-week ECG.
Use full 00947 capivasertib/fulvestrant when prescribed; 00361 remains monotherapy.
